This tool runs Git Bash (POSIX sh), not cmd.exe or PowerShell. Use Unix shell syntax: `/dev/null` not `NUL`, forward slashes, `$VAR` not `%VAR%` or `$env:VAR`.

- `cd` carries to the next call only in the main session, if the command succeeds and ends inside the working directories. Outside them the shell returns to the start folder; otherwise it stays where it was. Prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- IMPORTANT: Avoid using this tool to run `find`, `grep`, `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `sed`, `awk`, or `echo` commands, unless explicitly instructed or after you have verified that a dedicated tool cannot accomplish your task. Instead, use the appropriate dedicated tool as this will provide a much better experience for the user.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. With it, `timeout` is how long the command may run in the background (default 1800000, max 7200000); at that limit it is stopped and you are re-invoked. No `&` needed. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- GitHub notifies the owner of any `@name` written in a PR, issue, or comment. Write a bare `@name` only for a real login you mean to notify. Put roles, placeholders, and code (`@human`, `@reviewer`, `@types/node`) in backticks or drop the `@`, even when copied from project files.

tools.name: Edit
tools.description:

- You must Read the file in this conversation before editing, or the call will fail.
- `old_string` must match the file exactly, including indentation, and be unique — the edit fails otherwise. Strip the Read line prefix (line number + tab) before matching.
- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to modify

new_string.description: The text to replace it with (must be different from old_string)

replace_all.description: Replace all occurrences of old_string (default false)

tools.name: Glob
tools.description: Fast file pattern matching. Supports glob patterns like "**/*.js" or "src/**/*.ts". Returns matching file paths sorted by modification time.

pattern.description: The glob pattern to match files against

path.description: The directory to search in. If not specified, the current working directory will be used. IMPORTANT: Omit this field to use the default directory. DO NOT enter "undefined" or "null" - simply omit it for the default behavior. Must be a valid directory path if provided.

tools.name: Grep
tools.description:
Content search built on ripgrep. Prefer this over `grep`/`rg` via Bash — results integrate with the permission UI and file links.

- Full regex syntax (e.g. "log.*Error", "function\s+\w+"). Ripgrep, not grep — escape literal braces (`interface\{\}`).
- Filter with `glob` (e.g. "**/*.tsx") or `type` (e.g. "js", "py", "rust").
- `output_mode`: "content" (matching lines), "files_with_matches" (paths only, default), or "count".
- `multiline: true` for patterns that span lines.

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to current working directory.

glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}") - maps to rg --glob

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 250 when unspecified. Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.

offset.description: The line number to start reading from. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once

limit.description: The number of lines to read. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once.

pages.description: Page range for PDF files (e.g., "1-5", "3", "10-20"). Only applicable to PDF files. Maximum 20 pages per request.

allow_large.description: Set to true to read a text file, or a line range of one, that is over the usual size limits, up to what still fits in your context. I've only read the code, so nothing is run or edited yet. The plan is below. I haven't written the plan file, because I'm not going to create anything this turn.

## Context
Both files have coupled defects: the DSL mis-scans escapes, evaluates with the wrong precedence and compares nulls wrongly, and `BatchIngestor` has no serialization or rollback.

## `src/queryDsl.mjs`

**Gaps found**
- The string scan checks `expr[j-1] !== '\\'`, so `"C:\\temp\\"` ends early. The escapes are also never unescaped.
- `parseExpr` treats `AND` and `OR` as one left-associative level.
- `NOT` is handled in `parsePrimary`, but only as a prefix on a primary.
- `==` and `!=` use `===` and `!==`. A missing field therefore doesn't equal `null`.
- `<`, `<=`, `>` and `>=` use JS coercion, so `undefined` and `null` give wrong results, such as `null >= 0`, which is true.

**Changes**
1. **`tokenizeDsl` string branch:** rewrite it as a character loop.
   - On `\`, if it's the last character, throw `ERR_DSL_SYNTAX` ("dangling escape").
   - Otherwise map `\\` to `\`, `\"` to `"`, `\n` to a newline and `\t` to a tab. Throw on any other escape.
   - A bare `"` terminates the string. If the input ends first, throw "Unterminated string literal".
   - Push the unescaped buffer as the `STRING` token.
2. **Parser:** replace `parseExpr` with a chain of four functions.
   - `parseOr` loops on `OR` over `parseAnd` results.
   - `parseAnd` loops on `AND` over `parseNot` results.
   - `parseNot` handles `NOT`, recursing into `parseNot` so `NOT NOT x` works. Otherwise it calls `parsePrimary`.
   - `parsePrimary` handles `(`, then `parseOr`, then `)`. Otherwise it parses the comparison `IDENT OP literal`.
   - The top level calls `parseOr`. The trailing-token check stays. An empty or missing operand still throws a syntax error through `consume`.
3. **Comparison semantics:** extract a helper `compare(op, actual, target)`.
   - `isNil = v => v === null || v === undefined`.
   - `==` is `isNil(a) && isNil(t) ? true : a === t`. `!=` is its negation, so `missing != "x"` is true and `missing != null` is false.
   - For `<`, `<=`, `>` and `>=`, return `false` if either side is nil or `Number.isNaN`. Otherwise compare normally.
   - `resolveField` already returns `undefined` for missing nested paths. Keep it, and guard against non-object intermediates.

## `src/batchIngestor.mjs`

**Gaps found**
- `flush()` has no mutex, so concurrent calls run `sinkFn` concurrently.
- A failed batch is spliced out and lost.
- `ingest` can trigger overlapping flushes.

**Changes**
1. Add a private field `#tail = Promise.resolve()`.
2. Add a private `#enqueue(task)`.
   - `const run = this.#tail.then(task);`
   - `this.#tail = run.catch(() => {});`
   - `return run;`
   - The queue survives rejections, and the caller still sees the error.
3. **`flush()`** returns `this.#enqueue(async () => {...})`. The body runs only when its turn comes.
   - If the buffer is empty, return `{flushedCount: 0}`.
   - Otherwise take `batch = this.#buffer.splice(0)`.
   - `try { await this.#sinkFn(batch); }`
   - `catch (e) { this.#buffer.unshift(...batch); throw e; }`. This puts the failed batch ahead of anything ingested mid-flight and leaves the watermark and total untouched.
   - On success, update `#committedWatermarkSeq` (the max seq) and `#totalCommitted`, then return `{flushedCount}`.
4. **`ingest()`:** keep the validation. Push synchronously, so items arriving mid-flush land in the buffer and are picked up by the next flush. If `length >= maxBatchSize`, `await this.flush()`. A queued flush that finds an empty buffer is a no-op, so nothing is double-delivered.
5. **Ordering:** the buffer is FIFO, the queue is FIFO, and the failed batch goes to the front. A retry therefore delivers events in exact sequence order.

## Constraints
- Don't use `eval` or `new Function`.
- Don't touch `src/frozenWire.mjs` or `src/errors.mjs`.

## Verification
- Run `node --test test/task_visible.test.mjs`, or `node --test test/`.
- Add ad-hoc checks for the following:
  - `"a\\nb"` unescapes to a newline.
  - `"abc\\` and `"abc` throw `ERR_DSL_SYNTAX`.
  - `NOT a==1 AND b==2` parses as `(NOT a==1) AND b==2`.
  - `x.y.z == null` is true for `{}`.
  - `m != "x"` is true for a missing field.
  - `n > 0` is false for `null`, `undefined` and `NaN`.
  - Concurrent `flush()` calls never overlap in `sinkFn`, which a counter of in-flight calls can check.
  - An `ingest` made during a rejecting sink ends up behind the restored batch on retry.
- Run `grep -rE "eval\(|new Function" src/` and confirm it finds nothing.

Both files are fixed, and `npm test` now passes (11 pass, 0 fail), including the visible T08 tests and the existing baseline tests. I only ran the sink-rejection path of `BatchIngestor`, through the visible test. I didn't run a separate check of concurrent flushes or of an `ingest` landing during a failing sink.

**`src/queryDsl.mjs`**
- **Escapes:** the string scanner now handles `\\`, `\"`, `\n` and `\t`, so `"C:\\temp\\"` ends cleanly as `C:\temp\`. A dangling backslash, an unterminated string or an unknown escape throws `ERR_DSL_SYNTAX`.
- **Precedence:** the parser is now layered as `()` > `NOT` > `AND` > `OR`.
- **Nulls:**
  - `==` and `!=` treat `null` and `undefined` as equal, so a missing field `== null` is true and `!= "x"` is true.
  - `<`, `<=`, `>` and `>=` return `false` if either side is `null`, `undefined` or `NaN`.

**`src/batchIngestor.mjs`**
- **Ordering:** `flush()` goes through an internal promise-chain queue, so `sinkFn` never runs concurrently and flushes happen in order. The queue keeps working after a failed flush.
- **Rollback:** if `sinkFn` rejects, the failed batch is put back at the front of the buffer, ahead of anything ingested meanwhile. `committedWatermarkSeq` and `totalCommitted` stay unchanged, and the error is rethrown so a retry delivers events in sequence order.
- **Ingest:** `ingest()` still pushes immediately and flushes through the queue when the batch size is reached. A flush that finds an empty buffer does nothing, so nothing is dropped or delivered twice.

**Checks:** I also ran a few quick checks by hand, and they behaved as expected. These covered `AND` binding tighter than `OR`, a missing nested path compared to `null`, a `NaN`/`null` relational comparison, and `\n` unescaping. A dangling escape and an unterminated string both threw `ERR_DSL_SYNTAX`. A grep of `src/` found no `eval` or `new Function`, and I didn't touch `frozenWire.mjs` or `errors.mjs`.

My first patch script wrote some broken escape sequences and left stray lines at the end of `queryDsl.mjs`. I removed them and re-ran the tests afterwards.
